patient.name: Carla Beaumont
patient.chiefComplaint: Stab wound to left thigh with brisk, spurting bleeding

history.hpi: Bystanders report the patient was stabbed once in the left proximal thigh during an altercation approximately 8 minutes ago. She is conscious, anxious, and reports she 'can't stop the bleeding' despite holding a t-shirt against the wound. Blood is pooling rapidly on the pavement beneath her leg.
history.events: Assaulted with a knife during an altercation; bystanders called 911 immediately and attempted direct pressure with a t-shirt

scene.dispatch: 52-year-old female, stabbing, active bleeding, unknown weapon status
scene.location: Sidewalk outside a convenience store, urban area
scene.safety: Police on scene, assailant not located; scene marked as secure by law enforcement prior to EMS approach
scene.bystanders: Two bystanders present, one holding a blood-soaked t-shirt against the patient's thigh
visualCues: Large pool of blood on pavement beneath patient's left leg
Single stab wound to left proximal medial thigh, actively spurting bright red blood
Patient supine, pale, anxious, holding own leg
Blood-soaked improvised dressing in place from bystander
No other visible wounds on rapid body sweep

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 52-year-old female with an actively bleeding stab wound to the left proximal thigh. A bystander is holding direct pressure, but blood continues to spurt from beneath the dressing. Patient is alert but anxious, pale, and tachycardic.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak and rapid bilaterally, active spurting hemorrhage from left proximal thigh wound
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Strength intact in all extremities; unable to fully assess left leg distal perfusion due to ongoing hemorrhage
otherFindings: Active spurting bleeding from left proximal medial thigh despite bystander direct pressure
Large pool of blood on pavement
Patient anxious, repeatedly asking if she is going to die
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "It won't stop bleeding, please help me, I feel dizzy."

transitions.condition: Crew immediately recognizes life-threatening extremity hemorrhage on the MARCH primary survey and applies a commercial tourniquet proximal to the wound rather than continuing with direct pressure alone.
Crew continues with direct pressure and a pressure dressing alone despite ongoing brisk arterial bleeding, delaying tourniquet application.

phases.name: Tourniquet applied
phases.description: Crew applies a commercial tourniquet proximal to the wound, marks the application time, establishes IV access, and gives TXA and a fluid bolus targeting the trauma resuscitation blood pressure goal.
phases.triggerCondition: After recognizing life-threatening extremity hemorrhage on the primary survey, the crew applies a commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to the wound, stopping the bleeding and eliminating the distal pulse.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses weak but improving, tourniquet in place, bleeding stopped
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact proximal to tourniquet; distal pulse absent as expected with effective tourniquet
otherFindings: Commercial tourniquet applied 2-3 inches proximal to wound, bleeding stopped
Tourniquet application time marked on patient and documented
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "That hurts, but at least it's not gushing anymore."

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to wound until bleeding stops and distal pulse eliminated
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If the bleeding site is amenable to tourniquet placement, apply a commercial tourniquet to extremity: Tourniquet should be placed 2–3 inches proximal to wound, not over a joint, and tightened until bleeding stops and distal pulse is eliminated
expectedActions.rationale: Direct pressure alone has failed to control brisk arterial bleeding; a tourniquet is the definitive next step before shock worsens.

expectedActions.shortAction: Be prepared to apply a second tourniquet proximal to the first if bleeding continues, given the proximal thigh location
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If bleeding continues, place a second tourniquet proximal to the first. For thigh wounds, consider placement of two tourniquets, side-by-side, and tighten sequentially
expectedActions.rationale: Proximal thigh wounds may require a second tourniquet due to the large muscle mass and dual blood supply.

expectedActions.shortAction: Mark and document tourniquet application time prominently on patient and in the patient care report
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Mark the time of tourniquet placement prominently on the patient and in the patient care report
expectedActions.rationale: Tourniquet time is essential information for receiving trauma surgeons managing limb viability.

expectedActions.shortAction: Establish IV access and give TXA, within 3 hours of injury with signs of hemorrhagic shock
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Tranexamic acid (TXA) administration may be considered within three hours of injury and signs of hemorrhagic shock
expectedActions.rationale: This injury is well within the 3-hour window and the patient shows clear signs of hemorrhagic shock, meeting criteria for TXA consideration.

expectedActions.shortAction: Give 500 mL crystalloid bolus targeting SBP 90 mmHg since blood products unavailable
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If SBP less than 90 mmHg or HR greater than 120 BPM, initiate resuscitation: Blood products are recommended if available. If blood products not available, consider 500 mL bolus of IV fluid, repeat as needed for persistent signs and symptoms of shock. Trauma resuscitation target SBP 90 mmHg (palpable radial pulse or alert mental status)
expectedActions.rationale: SBP is below 90 mmHg, meeting the protocol threshold for fluid resuscitation toward the trauma target.

transitions.if: Bleeding controlled, TXA and fluids given
transitions.condition: Tourniquet remains effective, TXA and a fluid bolus have been given, and the patient's perfusion is improving. Crew prepares for rapid transport.
Crew loosens the tourniquet in response to the patient's pain, against protocol guidance not to loosen a tourniquet to relieve discomfort.

phases.name: Bleeding controlled, TXA and fluids given
phases.description: Hemorrhage is controlled with the tourniquet in place, TXA and a fluid bolus have been given, and the crew initiates rapid transport within the scene time goal while reassessing serially en route.
phases.triggerCondition: With bleeding controlled and TXA/fluids on board, the crew minimizes scene time and transports rapidly to the trauma center, reassessing the tourniquet and vitals frequently without removing the tourniquet.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses stronger, tourniquet remains effective, no active bleeding
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Sensation and movement intact proximal to tourniquet
otherFindings: Tourniquet time clearly marked and documented
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel a little less dizzy now. Thank you."

expectedActions.shortAction: Minimize scene time and initiate rapid transport to trauma center, goal under 10 minutes
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Minimize scene time (goal is under 10 minutes) and initiate rapid transport to the highest level of care within the trauma system
expectedActions.rationale: Penetrating trauma with major hemorrhage requires rapid surgical intervention; every minute on scene delays definitive care.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess tourniquet and vitals frequently en route without removing the tourniquet or dressing
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Without removing the tourniquet or dressing, reassess frequently for signs of ongoing or renewed bleeding, such as: Blood soaking through dressing, Bleeding distal to tourniquet
expectedActions.rationale: Continued vigilance ensures the tourniquet remains effective throughout transport without disturbing hemorrhage control.

phases.name: Tourniquet delayed, direct pressure only
phases.description: The crew continues with direct pressure and a pressure dressing alone despite ongoing brisk arterial bleeding, delaying the tourniquet. The patient's bleeding continues and perfusion worsens.
phases.triggerCondition: Direct pressure and a pressure dressing alone are attempted despite ongoing brisk arterial bleeding from the femoral wound, delaying tourniquet application beyond the point it should have been applied.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Radial pulses thready and rapid, blood continuing to soak through dressing
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Becoming difficult to assess as patient grows more anxious and weak
otherFindings: Blood actively soaking through pressure dressing
Growing pool of blood beneath patient
Patient becoming increasingly anxious and lightheaded
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: "I feel really dizzy... everything's getting fuzzy..."

expectedActions.shortAction: Recognize direct pressure has failed; apply commercial tourniquet 2-3 inches proximal to wound immediately
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: If direct pressure/pressure dressing is ineffective or impractical: If the bleeding site is amenable to tourniquet placement, apply a commercial tourniquet to extremity
expectedActions.rationale: Continuing direct pressure alone on ongoing arterial hemorrhage allows the patient to progress toward decompensated hemorrhagic shock.

phases.name: Tourniquet loosened for pain
phases.description: The crew loosens the tourniquet in response to the patient's pain complaints, against explicit protocol guidance. Bleeding resumes and perfusion worsens.
phases.triggerCondition: The tourniquet is loosened to relieve the patient's pain, despite the protocol explicitly stating not to loosen a tourniquet for pain relief, resulting in renewed hemorrhage.

clinicalPresentation.circulation: Renewed bleeding from wound site, pulses weakening again
otherFindings: Fresh blood visible at wound site after tourniquet loosened
Patient reports tourniquet pain prompted the request to loosen it

expectedActions.shortAction: Retighten tourniquet immediately; do not loosen for pain, treat pain with analgesics instead
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Properly-applied tourniquets in conscious patients are painful – treat pain with analgesics, but do not loosen a tourniquet to relieve discomfort. Do not loosen tourniquet to relieve pain
expectedActions.rationale: Loosening a tourniquet for pain reintroduces life-threatening hemorrhage; pain should be managed pharmacologically instead.
